construction: captured with ShroudForge's own mod runtime (a local differential test, not published): actual pinned ShroudForge mod-runtime, game-free private copies, release Windows x64 builds under headless Wine. Source checkouts were read-only. Every oracle transcript matched the shared sfi-core transcript host byte-for-byte.
scope: 18 callable IO functions (neither pin registers a nineteenth). Source-backed package bytes and independent predicates, owner-local alias identity, Windows lexical path grammar, exact return arity, raw export bytes and nonadvancing Buffer views, ordinary filesystem persistence and fresh-root boundaries. OS error text is not normalized. Injected-source ordering/per-entry warnings, virtual overlays, permissions, borrowed/closed/read-only Buffer states, owner capture and symlink/replacement hardening are additional source-derived host tests, not seeded-oracle observations. No game, archive format, engine service, source decompressor, native DLL or package discovery is implemented here.
parity_notes: Both implementations return raw bytes for read_to_string and read_export_to_string; parent never returns nil; export returns no values. list_files remains unsorted, while export_list sorts resolved paths.

Escape-only hardening: freeze configured root resolution before Lua, inspect all existing parents before mutation, pin directory traversal, disallow redirecting reparse/symlink replacements and use no-follow leaf opens. Contained symlink targets retain ShroudForge behavior. Windows self-resolving drive/mount reparses remain usable with pinned reparse handles. File/device reparses that bypass the selected root are refused.

Copy/rename atomically refuse destination replacement rather than clobbering a concurrently substituted destination. These checks affect only escape/replacement cases; ordinary in-sandbox results are preserved.

No panic: missing/nonabsolute host root configuration raises a Lua error rather than guessing a root or asserting/panicking. The explicit global flag is separate from root presence and from the package export capability.
